the development of a new generation of high performance, low latency track reconstruction systems for future experiments at the LHC, and in particular for the ATLAS upgrade.

the FTK is a powerful tool to improve the ATLAS physics reach in a wide variety of physics channels.

we are building a “baby” FTK, a “vertical slice” of the FTK system, to be used as an ATLAS detector element, to be integrated in a real ATLAS run, and to be operated as a part of the ATLAS data acquisition system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FTK hardware can already be used to exercise the ATLAS trigger system in the presence of full event data, and that the full FTK system can be realized with existing technology.
a “baby FTK” is a viable and valuable tool for testing and debugging the FTK hardware and software in the ATLAS computing environment, and for training the personnel in charge of the system.
the FTK system can be built and operated with a small fraction of the total resources, and that the system can be grown into a full functionality system with minimal changes.
